content.overview: BNS s. 47 — Abetment in India of offences outside India.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Abetment in India of offences outside India. BNS restatement of IPC 108A. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 108A. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 47 is the rule on “Abetment in India of offences outside India”. The section provides that a person abets an offence within the meaning of this Sanhita who, in India, abets the commission of any act without and beyond India which would constitute an offence if committed in India. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 47 exists so that “Abetment in India of offences outside India” has a closed legal test in Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: The inchoate trio. Abetment now covers extra-territorial aid; conspiracy and attempt sit next to it.

The provision in detail
47. A person abets an offence within the meaning of this Sanhita who, in India, abets the commission of any act without and beyond India which would constitute an offence if committed in India

Essential ingredients
1. A person abets an offence within the meaning of this Sanhita who, in India, abets the commission of any act without and beyond India which would constitute an offence if committed in India

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). A, in India, instigates B, a foreigner in country X, to commit a murder in that country, A is guilty of abetting murder

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 47 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.

learningObjectives: Analyze the cross-border jurisdiction under BNS s. 47.
Understand the extraterritorial nexus: act of abetment inside India targeting an offence outside India.
Apply the dual criminality standard: the targeted foreign act must constitute an offence if committed in India.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 47 provides that a person abets an offence within the meaning of this Sanhita who, in India, abets the commission of any act without and beyond India which would constitute an offence if committed in India.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Indian criminal jurisdiction prevents Indian territory from being utilized as a safe haven or planning hub for transnational crimes. A person who plans, instigates, or finances an offence from within India is punishable under Indian law, even if the physical crime is executed abroad.
statutoryFramework: Chapter IV — Of Abetment, Criminal Conspiracy and Attempt, BNS s. 47 (corresponding to IPC s. 108A).
Geographic nexus: The act of abetment (instigation, conspiracy, aiding) occurs 'in India'.
Target location: The act abetted takes place 'without and beyond India'.
Hypothetical test: The foreign act must be one which 'would constitute an offence if committed in India'.
essentialIngredients: The accused engaged in abetment within the territory of India.
The abetment was for the commission of an act outside India.
The act to be committed outside India is an offence under Indian penal law.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 47 establishes extraterritorial effect for preparatory and abetment acts committed on Indian soil. If a person residing in Mumbai conspires with, finances, or instigates a contract killer in Dubai to commit a murder in Dubai, the instigator cannot argue that Indian courts lack jurisdiction because the killing occurred outside Indian territory. Because the instigation took place within India, and murder is an offence under the BNS, s. 47 establishes full penal liability in Indian courts.
examples: Teaching example (Murder abroad): A, in India, instigates B, a foreign national in Nepal, to murder C in Nepal. A is guilty of abetting murder under s. 47.
Teaching example (Act not an offence in India): An act done abroad which is not an offence under Indian law cannot be the subject of abetment under s. 47.
distinctions: Abetment in India of foreign offences (s. 47) vs Abetment outside India for Indian offences (s. 48): Section 47 covers planning in India for execution abroad; Section 48 covers planning abroad for execution in India.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an individual in New Delhi who wired funds and instructions to an operative in London to bomb a commercial building can be tried in India.
Rule: BNS s. 47 penalizes anyone who, in India, abets an act outside India which would constitute an offence if committed in India.
Application: The financing and instructions originated in Delhi (India), and bombing a building is an offence of mischief by explosive substance under BNS.
Conclusion: Indian courts have full jurisdiction to try the individual under s. 47.
